title: Rewrite chat-template serialization to eliminate tokenizer mismatches during onboarding, pinflow, and profile publish
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: During recent model onboarding runs and several canary rollouts we observed tokenization drift between the onboarding harness, the pin-and-publish path, and the runtime chat serializer. This causes subtle role delimiter and escaped-character mismatches that lead to: (1) incorrect token counts in published performance profiles, (2) chat replay failures for pinned model variants, and (3) rare hallucination/regression flags in QA evals when templates are round-tripped.
problem_statement: The current chat-template serialization logic lives in three places: onboarding harness preprocessor, the pin/publish service, and the runtime adapter. Each implements slightly different delimiter normalization and escape rules (role markers, quoted spans, and whitespace collapse). When a model is onboarded with one normalization but pinned or served with another, the performance profile (token distribution and latency) no longer matches production behavior leading to bad policy choices (wrong batching/kv-cache heuristics) and customer surprises.
proposed_solution: 1) Consolidate serialization logic into a single shared library (chat-serialize) that implements a canonical normalization spec for delimiters, role escapes, and whitespace handling. 2) Replace onboarding, pin/publish, and runtime adapter usages with the shared library. 3) Add an explicit compatibility shim for legacy pinned profiles that records the onboarding serializer version and performs deterministic translation at publish time. 4) Publish a migration job to reconcile existing profiles (best-effort) and mark profiles that require manual review.
design_decisions: - Choose a deterministic, idempotent normalization that preserves user-provided role markers while encoding ambiguous whitespace as explicit tokens; this minimizes token-count delta. - Expose a serializer version field in model metadata so downstream services can detect mismatches. - Avoid silent automatic rewrites of pinned profiles without a review flag; add a 'reconcile' mode for safe migration.
work_breakdown: A. Implement chat-serialize library (Rust) + integration adapter (Node/Go bindings) - 3 pts; B. Replace onboarding preprocessor call sites and add serializer version capture - 1 pt; C. Update pin/publish flow to validate serializer compatibility and run shim translation - 1 pt; D. Migration job to reconcile existing profiles and a console flag for manual review - 2 pts; E. Tests and canary rollout - 2 pts.
acceptance_criteria: - Single shared serializer available as package and imported by onboarding, pin/publish, and runtime; - Tokens reported in newly published profiles match runtime tokenization within +/- 1 token for standard template set; - Serializer version captured in model metadata and surfaced in console; - Migration job produces reconciliation report and does not change profile values without a review flag; - No increase in customer-facing errors during a staged canary rollout.
testing_plan: Unit tests for normalization rules (role markers, escapes, unicode spacing); integration tests: onboarding -> publish -> runtime round trip with canonical template set; fuzz tests with varied templates and multi-lingual inputs; end-to-end smoke on dedicated staging cluster; canary rollout to 5% of traffic for two business days with automated metric checks (token-distribution drift, latency, error-rate).
